releaseNotes:
Changes since 0.3.0.

New collections:
- SchematiqHashSet: an unordered set.
- SchematiqOrderedHashSet: a set that keeps insertion order and can be indexed by position.
- SchematiqDictionary: an unordered dictionary.
- SchematiqOrderedDictionary: a dictionary that keeps insertion order, with access by position.
- SchematiqObject: an ordered dictionary of text keys, compared exactly, to values of any kind, like a JSON object. Edits return SchematiqObject, equality compares contents in any order, and ToString writes JSON. ISchematiqObject is its interface, which views implement too.
All four create and enumerate quickly, and make runs of single edits cheap. Each ordered interface extends its unordered one.

Ordered sets and dictionaries:
- Insert, AddBefore, AddAfter, RemoveAt, Move, MoveBefore and MoveAfter. A collection that never inserts before its end keeps its size and speed.

Read-mostly layout:
- CreateRange on all four hashed collections takes an optional SchematiqHashLayout. ReadMostly builds 256-entry hash leaves instead of 32-entry ones: a large set of integers keeps 25% less memory, and a dictionary of integers 19% less, with lookups and enumeration no slower. The first edits to each part of such a collection take up to twice as long and allocate up to three times as much, after which edits cost the usual.

Small collections:
- Sets and dictionaries of up to 8 entries are stored as plain arrays, and lists of 1 to 4 elements inline, so they are smaller and faster to create.
- Every collection has Compact, which rebuilds it in its smallest form.

SchematiqTable (preview):
- An immutable column-store table of named, typed, nullable columns, with rows readable as views.
- Expressions over columns, with SQL null logic: Filter, Calculate, Project, Rename, Sort, Distinct, Skip and Take.
- Pivot, with totals, ordering, a fill for empty combinations and named generated columns; and Unpivot, which keeps the columns' type where it can.
- Grouped and whole-table aggregates; inner, outer, semi, anti, condition and cross joins; Union, Intersect and Except.
- Row edits and Append; hash and sorted indexes, optionally unique, and a primary key that keeps the rows in order.
- Column and index names are compared exactly, case and all, as JSON compares an object's keys.
- TableRow.ToObject returns the row as an ISchematiqObject that reads the table in place.
- SchematiqTable.FromObjects makes a table over a list of your own objects, a column per property or chosen with ObjectColumn.
- SchematiqTableBase lets other kinds of table use every operator.

SchematiqList:
- SchematiqList.View returns a read-only list converted from another list, or computed from positions, as it is read: making one, Subset and Reverse cost nothing, and an edit copies it first.
- Create lists from spans and collection expressions.
- Faster indexing and enumeration, and cheaper SetItem, Insert and RemoveAt.
- Fixed Reverse after multi-item edits and after edits to double sequences, Subset of stems with part-filled leaves, and negative run lengths, which now throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException.

Serialization:
- SchematiqSerializer writes lists, sets and dictionaries (ordered ones in their order), Objects and tables to a compact binary format, and reads them back equal: tables with their schema, nulls, primary key and indexes (built again when read). Elements may be primitives, other Schematiq collections, or your own types through codecs (SchematiqCodec of T) registered by an id the file records, never a .NET type name.
- Repeated text is written once and referred to after; tables column by column with null flags; whole numbers, and numbers of up to six decimal places, as integers; dates of whole days or seconds as the change from the one before. A collection used more than once is written once and read back shared.
- Optional Deflate compression, or Brotli on .NET (not in the .NET Standard 2.0 build).
- Reading checks counts, lengths and nesting against limits in SchematiqSerializerOptions, and sets memory aside only as data arrives: damaged or hostile data throws SchematiqSerializationException.

Packaging:
- Targets netstandard2.0 and net8.0, with nullable annotations.
- The assembly is no longer strong-name signed.
